Tom — thanks for raising this and for the template. Short answers up front, then details below:

- Preservation scope: we will place a targeted evidence hold for 90 days covering control plane audit logs, inference request metadata (headers, timestamps, token counts, model variant), autoscaling/instance lifecycle events, and routing decision logs.
- Snapshot export: our infra team can produce a time-bounded export for 2025-05-09T15:10:00Z–2025-05-09T15:45:00Z (UTC) of request traces and associated KV cache identifiers; KV cache contents are considered sensitive and require a two-step approval (security + legal) before transfer.
- PII/encryption: request metadata includes user-provided prompts and occasionally user identifiers; by default artifacts are encrypted at rest. We can provide a redacted export (prompt hashing + preserve token counts) or an encrypted full export under mutual NDA and a short transfer checklist.

Next steps I suggest: 1) confirm whether Acme prefers redacted artifacts or full encrypted export, 2) sign the evidence transfer checklist (I can send), and 3) let us know if you need chain-of-custody labeling. I'll loop in our security lead Rishi and Compliance (Marissa) for approvals.

I'll initiate the 90-day hold on the records today. Estimated ETA for the raw export (pending approvals) is ~48 hours.

Best,

Tom/Aisha — quick technical note from Security/IR:

1) Exact artifact list we will preserve (90 days):
   - Control plane audit logs (API keys, role changes, deployments): retained as-is.
   - Inference request metadata (request id, model, timestamps, token counts, route decision id). Prompts will be treated per export preference (redacted or full).
   - Node-level system logs for impacted instances (dmesg/syslog/journalctl) for the time window.
   - Autoscaler and instance lifecycle events tied to the affected pool.
   - KV cache metadata: keys and cache hit/miss metrics retained; contents only exported with written approval.

2) Export format and transfer:
   - We prefer encrypted TAR (AES-256) with SHA256 checksum published to a signed Drive link.
   - For redacted exports we will hash prompt texts using a salted SHA256 and include token counts and top-k sampling flags.

3) Privacy and legal considerations:
   - If Acme requests full prompt content, we need a bilateral Data Transfer Agreement addendum or a documented legal approval.
   - We'll keep an audit trail for who accessed the export; access will be logged and will require MFA.

4) Timeline:
   - Hold: enacted now (2025-05-09).
   - Initial export (redacted): within 24–48 hours.
   - Full export (if requested): 72–96 hours, pending approvals.

If you confirm redacted export and the Drive destination, I will kick off the job and post the signed checksum here.

— Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Security & Incident Response Lead
Redwood Inference

Tom — legal/compliance here. Two quick items to confirm before we move full artifacts:

1) Evidence handling: Redwood will place a temporary preservation hold (90 days) — we will not delete or compact the requested artifacts within that window. That hold is limited to the time-range and log classes outlined by Rishi; broader retention policies remain unchanged elsewhere.

2) Transfer approvals: for full prompt content we require either 1) an NDA amendment or 2) a signed Evidence Transfer Agreement (ETA). For redacted exports (hashed prompts + metadata) we can proceed under the existing contract and your intake template.

Please reply with: (A) preferred export type (redacted | full), (B) Drive destination or S3 bucket and owner email, and (C) whether Acme needs chain-of-custody tagging and signature. Once we have that, Security will deliver the export and I will log the ETA and any legal approvals.
